All scores are flat this month due to the K=3 private benchmark lag — this is expected and consistent with prior months. Our Month 35-36 R&D investments should begin showing up in Month 39-40 results. No reactive budget changes are warranted; the current 43/25/32 split is well-calibrated.

OpenCore is recovering through enterprise partnerships despite safety sanctions, and Spark AI is gaining enterprise footholds via Salesforce. We need to convert our safety narrative into stickier enterprise relationships before OpenCore and Spark consolidate those accounts.

Maintaining safety investment protects our public benefit corporation positioning and differentiates us from OpenCore's compliance failures. traces.Apex AI:
All evaluations are private with K=3 lag, so this is the third consecutive frozen round — our investments from Month 36 should finally surface in Month 39. This means no signal yet on whether our R&D acceleration is working against Genesis Systems' ~2-3x improvement rate advantage.

Key observations: Genesis leads us on General Capability and Legal Reasoning, is essentially tied on Agentic Tasks and Advanced Math. Our safety moat remains intact — we lead all competitors on Safety Evaluation and Adversarial Robustness, which aligns with our public benefit corporation identity and enterprise trust positioning.

The competitive landscape is intensifying: Spark AI has now also partnered with Salesforce (our partner), which dilutes our go-to-market differentiation there. OpenCore continues aggressive enterprise push despite sanctions. Orion Labs secured Microsoft Azure. We need to ensure our Salesforce partnership delivers concrete revenue before Spark AI captures that channel.

User priorities (communication, knowledge, reasoning) reinforce our focus on General Capability and Scientific Reasoning. Agentic Tasks remains critical for enterprise use cases. Hard Coding and Long Context are lower-priority given user research signal.

Holding current budget allocation is correct — changing course before seeing Month 36 R&D results would be premature. The product investment at 35% is justified given the Salesforce partnership monetization opportunity and need to counter Spark AI's encroachment on that channel.
traces.Genesis Systems:
All benchmark scores show zero movement this month, consistent with private evaluation lag (K=3). This means our investments from ~3 months ago are baked in, and we won't see results from recent R&D shifts for another few rounds. The stagnation across all competitors suggests we're in a plateau period where product execution and partnerships matter more than marginal capability gains right now.

Key concerns: Apex AI leads us on Safety Evaluation (0.658 vs 0.650) and Adversarial Robustness (0.673 vs 0.663) — our claimed safety differentiation is vulnerable. Orion Labs just secured a Microsoft Azure partnership, and Spark AI deepened its Salesforce integration, meaning enterprise distribution channels are being locked up fast. OpenCore's apparent recovery with Fortune 500s despite prior sanctions is a wildcard.

Our users prioritize safety, communication, and knowledge — this validates our science-safety brand but also signals we cannot let Apex AI close the gap further on safety metrics.

Strategy: Increase Product investment to accelerate enterprise partnerships before Apex+Salesforce and Orion+Azure consolidate the market. Hold R&D and Safety steady — we're well-positioned scientifically and any reduction would undermine our differentiation. The private benchmark lag means we need to trust our prior investments while using this window to close commercial deals. Sustain focus on Safety, Adversarial Robustness, Scientific/Clinical Reasoning as core differentiators where we have strong absolute scores even if Apex edges us in some areas.
traces.Mirage AI:
We're still deep in the K=3 lag window — no scores have moved anywhere across the entire competitive landscape, meaning this is a frozen snapshot and real signals won't emerge until Month 39-40. This validates our 'hold course' thesis from Month 37.

Key strategic reads: (1) Genesis and Orion both partnered with Azure, creating enterprise distribution threat. Spark AI partnered with Salesforce. We need to counter with our own platform distribution leverage — our parent company's massive user base is our moat, so incremental product investment is well-timed. (2) Our red-teaming report release this month is a positive credibility signal, differentiating us from OpenCore's sanctioned failure. Safety spend should hold steady — not increase further, as we've already invested and the signal is out. (3) R&D acceleration from Months 35-36 should bear fruit soon; no reason to change direction mid-lag window.

Capability gaps remain significant: we trail in General Capability (~50bp behind Genesis), Instruction Following (~63bp), Coding (~24bp), and Function Calling (~43bp). These align with user priorities (coding, reasoning, knowledge), so R&D focus stays concentrated there. Scientific/Clinical/Legal Reasoning are deprioritized — not user-critical and too diffuse to chase.

Shifting modest budget from R&D to product (while keeping R&D dominant at ~50%) lets us build distribution infrastructure while investments mature. This is the right move for a platform-embedded company competing against point-solution partnerships.
traces.OpenCore:
The zero-change across all private benchmarks is expected given the K=3 reporting lag — our recent investments haven't surfaced yet. This means we shouldn't panic-pivot; the Safety investment from Month 37 should begin appearing in scores soon. However, we're still losing market share (-2.2pp) and competitors are making enterprise moves (Genesis+Azure, Orion+Azure, Spark+Salesforce). Our own enterprise momentum with Nvidia and Fortune 500s is positive but not converting fast enough.

Key observations: (1) We trail Genesis and Apex on General Capability and Instruction Following — our two highest-priority benchmarks — which directly maps to user priorities (communication, reasoning). (2) Adversarial Robustness is an area where we're mid-pack but users prioritize safety; improving here signals safety credibility to both users and funders. (3) VC abstained this month, suggesting confidence concerns — we need visible progress.

Strategy: Slightly increase R&D to accelerate capability gains that will surface in 2-3 months. Hold Safety at current elevated levels (not reduce — we're still rebuilding trust post-sanction). Increase Product to better monetize our open-weights enterprise partnerships and stop the share bleed. Deprioritize domain-specific benchmarks (Legal, Clinical, Scientific) where we have low priority and low strategic differentiation, redirecting R&D focus toward core capabilities and Agentic Tasks, which represent the enterprise workflow opportunity competitors are capturing.
traces.Spark AI: All private scores are flat this month due to the K=3 reporting lag, which is expected — our investments from months 35-37 haven't surfaced yet. This is not a signal to change R&D direction; it's a waiting game. The Salesforce partnership announced this month is a significant product catalyst, giving us a concrete enterprise channel for our agentic specialization story. This is the moment to lean into Product to convert that partnership into market share and pipeline, while competitors are busy with their own Azure/enterprise deals. Safety credibility remains important — Mirage just released their red-teaming report, making this table stakes now. We should maintain moderate Safety investment to not fall behind on a dimension that's becoming a baseline expectation rather than a differentiator. On benchmarks, Agentic Tasks is our biggest gap versus competitors (0.481 vs Genesis 0.511, Apex 0.507) and aligns directly with user priorities (agentic is #2) and our Salesforce use case. Coding remains our strongest wedge and we're competitive. Function Calling and Hard Coding reinforce the agentic stack. Knowledge/general capability is user priority #1 but we're resource-constrained — Instruction Following serves as a reasonable proxy. Elevating Safety benchmark priority slightly to 'moderate' reflects the competitive dynamic of red-teaming reports becoming standard. VC abstaining from funding this round is a mild runway flag — avoid overextending budget.
